classification_scope: This is an R3 evidence classification for Project OS audit. It is not a Gate 7 GO, integration result, Gate 5 completion, live-release approval, or overall production-readiness claim.

historical_build.subject: Publish universal trip visualizer and Pages workflow

r2_final.role: QA/evidence tail only; not product-source authority

identity_proof.checkout_controls: Source candidate and historical build commit were inspected in clean isolated detached worktrees outside the repository.

r2_tail_proof.interpretation: The R2 tail is QA/evidence only. No product source, runtime source, workflow, dependency pin, manifest, or vendored-runtime path changed between the immutable source candidate and R2 final.

bundle.tracked_build_metadata_boundary: The historical tree contains no package.json, package-lock.json, yarn/pnpm lock, .tools/jsdeps tree, node_modules tree, or bundler configuration. Tracked build scripts consume the already-tracked vendor bundle and do not reconstruct this JS workspace.

provenance_recovery.registry_search_method: npm registry release metadata was queried for all stable semver releases of each named package at or before the historical commit cutoff; prereleases and post-cutoff releases were excluded. The latest eligible release for each package was tested first because the source uses plain package imports and the bundle fingerprints identify the package module boundaries.
candidate_exclusion_logic: Post-cutoff releases and prereleases were excluded as historically impossible.
The source has no semver selectors or tracked lock to justify arbitrary older versions.
The exact byte match is decisive; API resemblance, exports, file size, and partial source similarity were not accepted as proof.
Minified output was tested and rejected because its bytes/hash did not match the tracked bundle.
provenance_recovery.workspace: Temporary workspace outside the repository; historical src/vector_entry.js was copied in, exact package tarballs were installed under .tools/jsdeps, and node_modules resolution was linked to that isolated workspace.

reproduction.decisive_result: Exact byte and SHA-256 reproduction succeeded.

playwright.archive_integrity_limitation: The inspected Playwright package browsers.json/coreBundle.js define revisions, browser versions, archive paths, and mirrors, but do not expose SHA-256/integrity values for downloaded browser archives. install --list reports cache identities only. No archive hash is claimed or fabricated.
playwright.provenance_disposition: Pinned Python package plus package-defined browser revisions/build identifiers are exact and reproducible; archive-hash absence is recorded as a limitation, not an unresolved version boundary.

components.runtime_exposure: Embedded in shipped trip-vector bundle; advisory is relevant and exact version is at patched boundary.

browser_review_limits: No exact Chromium 151.0.7922.34 CVE was identified in the authoritative sources reviewed; this is not a universal clean bill.
The Apple Safari 26.5 advisory surface was not treated as an exact Playwright WebKit-build match; no unsupported equivalence was claimed.
Playwright and Playwright-Python maintainer advisory pages had no published advisories at review time.

recorded_limitations: Playwright browser archive SHA/integrity values are not exposed by the inspected authoritative package metadata.

The historical repository did not track the JS dependency workspace or lock; exact provenance is established by registry identities plus independent byte/hash reproduction, not by a historical lockfile.
Current advisory review is bounded to the authoritative sources and exact versions listed above; absence from one advisory API is not treated as universal cleanliness.
residual_items.disposition: No material Gate-7 exact-dependency-provenance requirement remains unresolved for the shipped trip-vector runtime or the package-defined Playwright browser revisions.

final_policy.not_fix_required: No known material vulnerability was found in the shipped runtime bundle at the exactly reproduced component versions. The Firefox 153.0 advisory is explicitly QA-only and is not a shipped product runtime finding.
